cohort: The study included 330 women who were administered questionnaires prenatally and at 3-4 days and 4 months postpartum.
finding: Impaired breastfeeding initiation was strongly predicted by neonatal NICU admission, high maternal BMI, cesarean section, difficulties with initiation, and high maternal state anxiety, while impaired maintenance was predicted by maternal smoking, high BMI, and a history of postpartum anxiety disorder.
mod_finding: Cesarean section was identified as a strong predictor of impaired breastfeeding initiation.
